chunks: As for the voluntary prayers, they are twice the like of the obligatory ones at thirty-four units: eight units before Dhuhr, and eight after it before Asr, and four units after Maghrib, and two units while sitting after the final Isha - counted as a single unit, and it serves as the witr for whoever did not perform the witr at the end of the night,
and the night prayer is eight units, every two units with a taslima, and the shafʿ is two units with a taslima, and the witr is a single unit, and the voluntary prayer of Fajr is two units.
So the total of the obligatory and voluntary prayers in the day and night is fifty-one units.

key_terms.الشفع: Shafʿ prayer, a pair of units performed before the witr
key_terms.النافلة: Voluntary/supererogatory prayer (nafilah), performed in addition to the 17 obligatory units
key_terms.تسليمة: Taslima, the concluding salutation (salam) that ends a prayer set
key_terms.وتر: Witr prayer, an odd-numbered unit performed individually

ai.seo_question: How many voluntary (nafilah) prayer units are there in Shia Islam, and when are they performed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq details the structure of the voluntary (nafilah) prayers according to Shia jurisprudence. The text enumerates 34 units of voluntary prayers distributed across the five daily prayer times, including the night prayer (salat al-layl) and its components (shafʿ and witr). This passage was transmitted in the context of a scholarly assembly in 368 AH and represents the well-established Shia legal position that the total daily prayers - obligatory and voluntary combined - amount to 51 units.

en.bilal-muhammad: As to the voluntary prayers, then they are twice the like of obligation at thirty-four units: eight units prior to Thuhr, eight units after it prior to `Asr, four units after Maghrib, two units while sitting after the final `Isha – counted as a single unit, and it is the witr for whoever did not make the witr at the end of the night –
and the night salat is eight units, each being two units with a taslima, the shaf` is two units with a taslima, the witr is a single unit, and the voluntary prayer of Fajr is two units.
So, the sum total of the obligatory and the voluntary prayers in the day and night is fifty-one units.
